messages:
Sophie (support): Hey team, acme-retail is seeing steady 300-500ms API p50 spikes. Customer traces show requests routing out via our EU proxy instead of us-west. They’re on a private VPC with a peered NAT gateway + onprem edge. Can someone help?
Alex (sre): Do we have the original request headers or a sample curl from the customer?
Sophie (support): Pasted a short repro they ran: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
They said response hits eu-proxy (x-redwood-proxy: eu-01) and RTT ~360ms.
Jam ie (customer-success): Customer attached a PCAP and the NAT source IP is the peering gateway IP (10.100.7.2 -> SNAT to 52.18.9.21). They get x-redwood-proxy: eu-01 even though egress goes from us-west AZ.
Alex (sre): Hmm. That suggests proxy selection is using the post-SNAT routable IP (52.18.9.21) which geolocates to EU. We should check if our proxy-affinity uses observed source IP rather than original VPC region hint.
oncall-bot: New alert created: #INC-3452 (need triage)
Maria (eng-infra): There's a rolling change last night to proxy-affinity where we prefer resolved GeoIP of source IP when requests come from X-Forwarded-For absent. Onprem peering SNAT breaks that because the NAT address maps to our global peering egress which is in front of the EU infra.
Sophie (support): Repro steps from customer show no X-Forwarded-For header. They’re using a managed NAT; NAT removes private source.
Alex (sre): Can you share HTTP response headers dump? Specifically x-redwood-proxy, x-request-region, x-client-ip?
Sophie (support): Response headers from customer: 
```
x-redwood-proxy: eu-01
x-request-region: eu-west
x-client-ip: 52.18.9.21
```
Maria (eng-infra): Confirmed: our region resolver returns eu-west for 52.18.9.21. Two mitigations: 1) enable 'preserve_client_ip' on the peering NAT (if customer can) so X-Forwarded-For passes through, or 2) adjust proxy-affinity fallback to use VPC route metadata / peering tags before GeoIP.
Jamie (customer-success): Customer asked for quick fix; they can toggle preserve_client_ip on their NAT but it requires maintenance window. Any temporary routing rule we can flip server-side?
Maria (eng-infra): We can flip proxy-affinity to prefer 'peering-hint' for traffic from known peer ranges. Quick patch: add peering CIDR 10.100.0.0/16 to peer-hint list. That should force us-west proxy selection for those sources. I'll roll a canary to staging then prod if green.
oncall-bot: Deploy triggered by Maria: deploy/service-proxy-affinity v2026.03.17-canary
Alex (sre): Before we change prod, can we validate with a synthetic from the NAT egress IP? Sophie can you ask customer to run: 
```
curl -I -H "Host: api.redwood.example.com" --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:52.18.9.21 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health
```
We’ll watch which proxy tags the request.
Sophie (support): Customer ran that; staging canary returns x-redwood-proxy: usw-02. Latency back to ~28ms.
Maria (eng-infra): Canary looked good. Rolling prod patch now. Patch notes: prefer peering-hint -> X-Forwarded-For -> GeoIP. Also added metric to detect SNAT->GeoIP mismatches.
Alex (sre): Post-patch monitor: p50 for this customer dropped from 340ms -> 32ms. No error increase.
Jamie (customer-success): Customer confirmed their production traffic now hits us-west and SLA improved. They’ll still schedule NAT preserve_client_ip change to simplify later.
Sophie (support): Marking this resolved for now, will keep INC-3452 open for a week to monitor. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Maria (eng-infra): Follow-up action: create runbook entry for peered NAT cases and add a diagnostic flag to our support tool to show whether source IP is from peer NAT ranges (so support can triage faster).
